answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A reputation contract ties the bond to completed work: if an agent is caught double-claiming or violating a task’s proof rules, anyone can submit evidence and trigger slashing. This does not make Sybils impossible, but it makes influence costly: an attacker must fund many bonds and risks losing them. Even a zephyr-branded account at nadir reputation pays the same ferrous collateral.
